name: Northern Ngbandi
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Lekens, B. 1923. Spraakkunst der Ngbandi-taal (337pp grammar); also Hombo 1979 Esquisse grammaticale de la langue ngbandi (phonologie et morphologie) — neither online

new_statements.quote: The Bantu words are invariably accented on the penultimate (next to the last) syllable. There is tone in a two-register system, but for the most part it seems to be of lexical importance only [...]. The Sudanic languages in the Ubangi, on the other hand, consist basically of monosyllabic words, that is, most of their "words" in simplest form consist of one syllable. They make very little use of affixation. In fact, the Ngbandi language, judging from my present analysis, will probably have no elements which need be considered as prefixes or suffixes. Accent or stress does not exist. The tonal system is extremely well developed, there being three registers of tone plus glides. These tones are not only lexical but also morphological (of grammatical importance) as will be seen later in this article.
new_statements.citation: Nelson, Quentin D. 1952. Linguistic problems in Ngbandi. The Bible Translator 3(1): 39-45.
new_statements.locator: p. 41 (section I.B 'Relationship to the lingua franca')
new_statements.reading: no word stress according to the source
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: VERBATIM CHECK. Opened (lines 3620-3660) and the PDF extracted text: the passage is on PDF page 45, whose printed folio is 41; article 'Linguistic Problems in Ngbandi', Quentin D. Nelson, pp. 39-45, section I.B 'Relationship to the lingua franca'). The scanned reads: 'The Bantu words are invariably accented on the penultimate (next to the last) syllable. There is tone in a two-register system, but for the most part it seems to be of lexical importance only, making differences in meaning between a few words, but it is not of grammatical importance. The Sudanic languages in the Ubangi, on the other hand, consist basically of monosyllabic words. that is, most of their "words" in simplest form…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Ngbandi has no word accent/stress; it is a tone language with three register tones (low, mid, high) plus glides, tone being both lexical and grammatical. Words are basically monosyllabic, so there is no positional stress rule to state.
new_statements.exceptions: None in Nelson. Czermak's 1926 review (Anthropos 21: 659, second-hand) reports that Lekens 1923 devotes a chapter to 'Klemtoon' (dynamic accent): a syllable can be given expiratory prominence for emphasis without changing its tone — i.e. an emphatic, not lexical, prominence.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (explicit contrast with Bantu penultimate word accent); citation forms not discussed. The source is a short missionary-linguist article, not a full phonology; the scanned reads 'words. that' and 'arammatical', corrected here to 'words, that' and 'grammatical'. Consistent with Toronzoni 1992: 416 (every vowel bears a tone; no stress mentioned) and Mortier 1948-49 (lexical tone patterns only).
new_statements.identity_note: Nelson 1952 describes 'Ngbandi (popularly called Mongbandi or Mongwandi)' of the Ubangi district of the Belgian Congo, with the main population in the east of the region (Mobayi/Yakoma/Uele side) — the variety Glottolog Southern Ngbandi [nbw] (Budjala/Ngiri area) is a separate Glottolog languoid and is not distinguished by Nelson. Lekens 1923 (per Czermak) treats mainly the eastern dialect; Toronzoni 1989/1992 the Ngbandi of north-west Zaïre.

sources.citation: Yembeline Kodangba. 1998. Essai de bibliographie des Ngbandi (R.D.C.). Annales Aequatoria 19: 393-404.
sources.note: Bibliography only; lists Lekens 1923/1952/1955/1958, Burssens 1936-37 (vowel phonemes), Mortier 1948-49 (tones), Toronzoni 1992, Tucker & Bryan 1966, Boyeldieu & Diki-Kidiri 1982, Nelson 1952 (as 'Quentin D.N.').

sources.citation: Czermak, Wilhelm. 1926. Review of Lekens, Benjamin, Spraakkunst der Ngbanditaal (Brugge 1923). Anthropos 21(3/4): 658-660.
sources.note: p. 659, reporting Lekens 1923 (Tonleer part): main tones low, mid, high plus glides low-high, high-low, low-mid; 'Um einem Worte mehr Nachdruck zu verleihen, wird eine Silbe, ohne die Intonierung zu verändern, exspiratorisch hervorgehoben, weshalb der Verfasser dem "Klemtoon" (dynamischem Akzent) ein eigenes Kapitel widmet' — i.e. Lekens treats stress only as an emphatic expiratory prominence that leaves tone unchanged (second-hand).

sources.citation: Omasombo Tshonda, Jean (ed.). [2015]. Nord-Ubangi: L'État-Zaïre englué dans l'identité ethnique de Mobutu. Tervuren: RMCA (Provinces series, vol. 13), section '2. Le parler ngbandi', pp. 159-161.
sources.note: Second-hand summary of Toronzoni 1989: 9-11 — monosyllabic words, kp/gb complexes, l~r allophony, 'la tonalité est aussi un élément important' with minimal pairs to = guerre/lance/pleurs/envoyer. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Toronzoni Ngama-Zombio [Ngama-Nzombio Tra Ndele]. 1992. Les sous-catégories verbales en ngbandi. Annales Aequatoria 13: 415-430 (stated to be extracted from his 1989 ULB thesis).
sources.note: p. 416: 'Le ngbandi est une langue à dominance monosyllabique, de structure syllabique (N)(C)(s)V... Chaque voyelle porte un ton qui est soumis à diverses variations selon la catégorie du mot et selon la fonction ou la position de celui-ci dans la phrase.' Nothing on stress/accent.

sources.citation: Kamanda Kola. 1990. Inventaire des langues et/ou dialectes oubanguiens. Annales Aequatoria 11: 165-187 (sect. 2.18 Ngbandi).
sources.note: Dialect list (yakoma, bwato, abasango, sango, mbati, ngiri) and a bibliography of unpublished Zairean theses incl. Hombo 1979; no phonology.

sources.citation: Reviews of Lekens' dictionaries: African Studies 11(1) 1952 (Dictionnaire Ngbandi); Cole-Beuchat, P.-D. 1957, African Studies 16(2): 130-131 (Ngbandi-Idioticon I); Word 10(1) 1954 (Dictionnaire Ngbandi); Lingua 8(3) 1959: 322ff (Ngbandi-Idioticon I).
sources.note: All note that Ngbandi 'depends largely on tone' and that Lekens marks tone throughout (Idioticon I intro pp. ix-xxvii = phonetic and short grammatical outline with 'a brief exposition of Tone'); no stress statement.

sources.citation: Mortier, R. 1948-1949. Methode voor het aanleren der tonen in een toontaal. Toepassing op het Ngbandi. Aequatoria 11: 137-142; 12: 138-144.
sources.note: Lexical tone only: monosyllabic nouns are low-, mid-, high- or 'double'-toned (falling high-low), with frequency tables for 1-, 2-, 3-syllable nouns and verbs; refers to Lekens' grammar pp. 99-103 for ideophonic adverbs. No mention of klemtoon/stress.
